Introduction to herdr

Introduction.Rmd

Welcome to herdr

herdr is an integrated computational framework in R for modeling greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, feed environmental footprints & water deprivation, agricultural land competition, and nutritional edible protein across livestock production systems.

Most existing calculators evaluate emissions or feed land requirements in isolation. herdr bridges animal physiology, nutritional energy balances, herd demography, manure management, and international trade flows into a single, internally consistent modeling engine.

Core Capabilities 

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                 herdr ENGINE OVERVIEW                                  │
├──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┤
│  1. IPCC TIER 2 GHGs     │  2. AGROECOLOGICAL LAND     │  3. FOOD PRODUCTIVITY & FCR   │
│  • Enteric CH4           │  • Cropland vs Grassland    │  • GLEAM Milk, Meat, Eggs     │
│  • Manure CH4            │  • Mottet (2017) Framework  │  • IDF (2022) Physical Alloc. │
│  • Direct & Indirect N2O │  • FAOSTAT Bilateral Trade  │  • Mottet (2017) Protein FCRs │
├──────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┤
│  4. UPSTREAM FEED LCA & WATER DEPRIVATION (EF 3.1)                                     │
│  • ECOALIM v9 & AGRIBALYSE v3.1 (Fossil vs. LUC CO2e)                                  │
│  • AWARE Freshwater Deprivation (m3 depriv. / Mm3 depriv.)                             │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  1. IPCC Tier 2 Greenhouse Gas Inventories: Implements the 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories for ruminants (cattle, sheep, goat) and monogastrics (swine, poultry, adopting FEDNA nutritional standards).
  2. Agroecological Land Footprint & Competition: Quantifies feed land requirements (m2\text{m}^2) and classifies land according to human food competition (Mottet et al., 2017) into Cropland, Convertible Grassland, Unconvertible Rangeland, and None. When ingredient origins are unspecified, herdr traces true producer countries using recursive FAO bilateral trade matrices and national self-sufficiency thresholds.
  3. Animal Productivity & Edible Human Protein: Implements the FAO methodology to translate herd throughput across functional roles (mature, replacement, slaughter) into physical commodities (Fat and Protein Corrected Milk, cold dressed carcass weight, boneless meat, greasy wool, and fresh eggs) and total digestible human protein (kg protein/year).
  4. Enterprise Attribution, Biophysical Co-Product Allocation & Protein Feed Efficiency: Automatically integrates non-commercial rearing and breeding overheads (replacement and mature breeders) into commercial outputs, applies the International Dairy Federation (IDF Bulletin 520/2022) Net Energy physical allocation, and reports protein conversion and human food competition metrics (Protein_FCR_total and Protein_FCR_cropland).
  5. Upstream Feed LCA & Water Deprivation (EF 3.1 / AWARE): Integrates INRAE/ADEME ECOALIM v9 to evaluate upstream feed carbon footprints (fossil emissions vs. deforestation LUC) and freshwater deprivation (m3 depriv.\text{m}^3\text{ depriv.}) characterized via the international AWARE model.

Supported Livestock Species & Canonical Taxonomy

herdr natively supports full life cycles across five major domestic species using a strict, standardized taxonomy:

  • 🐄 Cattle (cattle | dairy or meat): Mature dairy cows (mature), suckler beef cows and breeding bulls (mature), replacement calves and yearling heifers (replacement), and feedlot/beef fattening calves (slaughter).
  • 🐑 Sheep (sheep | dairy or meat): Dairy ewes, meat ewes, and breeding rams (mature), replacement lambs (replacement), and slaughter lambs (slaughter).
  • 🐐 Goats (goat | dairy or meat): Dairy does, meat does, and bucks (mature), replacement kids (replacement), and dairy/meat fattening kids (slaughter).
  • 🐖 Swine (swine | meat): Breeding sows and service boars (mature), replacement gilts (replacement), and fattening pigs (slaughter).
  • 🐔 Poultry (poultry | meat or layer): Commercial laying hens and free-range layers (layer / mature), layer replacement pullets (layer / replacement), meat breeder hens (meat / mature), meat replacement pullets (meat / replacement), and broilers (meat / slaughter).

Quick Start: Choose Your Path

herdr can be operated either through an interactive web-based graphical interface (GUI) or programmatically via R scripts.

Option A: Interactive Web Application (No Coding Required) 

library(herdr)

# Initialize local workspace with templates
herdr_init()

# Launch the interactive Shiny interface
run_herdr_app()

The Shiny app provides guided forms, strict dropdowns, real-time pre-flight validation, interactive stacked charts, and one-click CSV/PNG downloads. See the Interactive App Guide for a complete walkthrough.

Option B: Scripted R Pipeline (Reproducible Research) 

library(herdr)

# 1. Initialize local project directories and templates
herdr_init()

# 2. Run consolidated environmental and nutritional assessment
results <- generate_impact_assessment(
  farm_country = "Spain",
  year         = 2024,
  gwp_report   = "AR5"
)

# Inspect Table 1 (Cohort Totals) and Table 2 (Enterprise Product Intensities)
results$totals
results$intensities

# 3. Visualize results across impact categories and functional units
p <- plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = c("animal_type", "region"),
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "ghg",
  functional_unit = "protein" # kg CO2e per kg edible protein
)

print(p)

See the Scripting Workflow for complete step-by-step instructions.
